meta.title: Horotachi Ski Area
meta.description: 44° powder in Horokanai—local slopes and buckwheat soba after the runs, via Asahikawa Airport.

transit.title:
From Asahikawa,
over the pass.
transit.lead: About 60 minutes from downtown Asahikawa, roughly two hours by rental car from Asahikawa Airport via the Chichibubetsu IC. Mountain weather can change fast—check road conditions before you cross the pass.
transit.imgAlt: Car on a snowy road—winter drive from Asahikawa to Horokanai

primary.title: 44° ungroomed lines
primary.lead: The Horotachi course hits 44° on ungroomed snow. Deep snowfall and natural terrain draw riders who want steep, quiet powder—one 635 m pair lift and almost no queues.
primary.imgAlt: Skier on steep ungroomed powder at Horotachi

secondary.title: After the runs: soba
secondary.lead: Horokanai is Japan's top buckwheat region. Hit a town soba shop after skiing—the hill cafeteria and local noodle houses are the post-run ritual.

onsen.title:
After skiing,
Sounkyo on the way back.
onsen.lead: Hot springs in Horokanai town are limited, but Sounkyo and Kamikawa onsen cluster along the drive back to Asahikawa.
onsen.whisper: If pass weather turns, heading down early may beat a long soak. Always follow official road and facility updates.
onsen.imgAlt: Snow-view outdoor bath—Sounkyo area hot spring image

powder.title: Chasing 44° powder
powder.body: Four courses, one pair lift. Horotachi is advanced ungroomed; the forest course is a 1,100 m beginner groomer—small in scale, big on pitch and snow quality.

drive.title: From Asahikawa Airport
drive.body: Pick up a rental at Asahikawa Airport and follow National Route 275 toward Horokanai. About 60 minutes from downtown Asahikawa; roughly two hours from the airport.

soba.title: Soba and town food
soba.body: Horokanai soba is the local star. Pair the hill cafeteria with a town noodle shop for a half-day food loop.

access.note: About 60 min by car from Asahikawa; about 60 min from Chichibubetsu IC via Route 275 (estimate)
